title: Pjama map
description: A Pjama project map: the components of a project, the specs they hold and the relationships between them. This schema checks types only: cardinality, references between items and other cross-item rules are checked by the schema validator, not here.

$schema.description: Location of this JSON Schema, for editors and tools. It doesn't state which version of the map model the map follows: see schemaVersion.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the map model the map is written in, as v<MAJ>.<MIN>.<PATCH>.

slug.description: Derived from the name: diacritics dropped keeping the base letter, symbols other than letters, digits and spaces removed, repeated spaces collapsed, letters lowercased and the remaining spaces turned into hyphens.

root.description: Path from the folder holding the map to the root of the project, in POSIX format. Every other path in the map is relative to this root.

relationships.description: Every relationship of the map, of any type.

checks.description: Every check of the map, of any type. Check results, states and reviewers are not stored in the map.

actors.description: Every actor of the map, shared by the use cases that list them.

item.description: Fields shared by every object that lives in the map.

id.description: Random UUID identifying the item. Item ids never collide.

type.description: Type of the item, which decides its other fields.

component.description: A piece of the project, holding its own specs.

specs.description: The specs the component holds. Each spec belongs to this component only, and reaches other components through relationships.

resources.description: Ids of the resources supporting the component. Resources don't take part in spec flows.

specBase.description: Fields shared by every spec. A spec states a constraint on the component that holds it.

category.description: Free-form category. The map's categories are the set of those used across its specs.

requirement.description: An atomic statement about the component.

useCase.description: A sequence of actions pertinent to the component.

actors.description: Ids of the actors taking part in the use case.

prerequisites.description: Conditions or properties assumed to hold for the use case to apply.

steps.description: The steps of the use case. Linked through next and sibling, they form a directed acyclic graph with a single root, where the sequence starts.

step.description: One specific action of a use case.

id.description: Random UUID identifying the step within its use case.

next.description: Id of the step that follows. Pointing to a step of another branch merges into it. Without it, the sequence terminates here.

sibling.description: Id of the first step of an alternative branch, taken instead of this step.

interface.description: A contract with inputs and outputs. Its types are the ones visible to its component: its own and the ones reaching it through flows.

name.description: The parameter's name. Inputs are always named.
The output's name, when it has one, e.g. for a named return value.

preconditions.description: Conditions that hold before the interface is invoked.

postconditions.description: Conditions that hold after the interface is invoked.

invariants.description: Conditions that hold before and after the interface is invoked.

protocols.description: Protocols used to invoke the interface, e.g. HTTP or CLI.

snippet.description: Business logic given as a code snippet, in pseudocode or a real language.

language.description: Language the body is written in. Without it, the body is pseudocode.

typeSpec.description: A custom type. Its name is unique only within its component, and it reaches other components through flows like any other spec.

typeExpression.description: The shape of a type, which may contain other type expressions. A type may refer to itself.

name.description: Free-form primitive name, e.g. string or int64, so the map isn't tied to one language's type system.

type.description: Id of a type spec visible to the referencing spec's component.

optional.description: Whether the field may be absent. Fields are required by default.

mergeType.description: All the fields of several structs, together.

constantType.description: A single value. Distinct from a custom type.

value.description: The value written as a raw literal, e.g. "foo" with its quotes, or 42.

mockup.description: A visual reference for a piece of UI, from a rough wireframe to a high-fidelity design.

resource.description: Id of the resource holding the image, in any format a browser can display (e.g. PNG, JPEG, SVG, WebP).

body.description: Inline HTML: a fragment of elements, rendered inside a blank HTML document, or a full HTML document. It is rendered isolated from the app displaying it, and its scripts are blocked from execution.

resource.description: Id of the resource holding a full HTML document. It is rendered isolated from the app displaying it, and its scripts are blocked from execution.

technology.description: A technology, such as a language, framework or library, that the component is built with or must use.
Name of the technology, e.g. TypeScript. Separate from the spec's own name.

version.description: Version or version range of the technology, in free form.

documentation.description: Ids of the resources documenting the technology.

actor.description: Someone or something taking part in use cases.

resource.description: Supporting material: a file inside the project or a page at a URL. Resources don't take part in spec flows.

location.description: Path of a file inside the project, relative to the project root in POSIX format, or a URL.

decision.description: A choice made about the project, why it was made and why the other options weren't. Its status is derived, not stored: overridden if another decision overrides it, otherwise closed if it is marked closed or has a chosen option, otherwise open.

closed.description: Marks the decision closed, also when none of its options is chosen.

chosenOption.description: Id of the chosen option. Choosing an option closes the decision.

rationale.description: Why the chosen option was picked over the others.

references.description: Ids of the items pertinent to the decision.

overrides.description: Ids of earlier conflicting decisions this one overrides. They stay in the map.

id.description: Random UUID identifying the option within its decision.

review.description: A manual check, assessed by a human or an agent. Its results and reviewers are not stored in the map.

criteria.description: Statements the reviewed work must satisfy to pass.

resources.description: Ids of the resources to look at.

instructions.description: How to carry out the review, as free-form text rendered as markdown.

reviewer.description: Who must perform the review. Without it, either may.

test.description: An automated, repeatable check run by a plugin. Its results are not stored in the map.

plugin.description: Name of the plugin that runs the test, e.g. @pjama/vitest-test.

config.description: Plugin-specific settings, validated by the plugin's own schema.

relationshipBase.description: A directed edge from a source item to a target item. Relationships are not items: they have no name or description.

type.description: Type of the relationship, which decides what source and target are.

source.description: Id of the item the edge starts from: the one that depends on the target.

target.description: Id of the item the edge points to.

containment.description: The source component (child) is part of the target component (parent). All specs pass both ways.

dependency.description: The source component (consumer) uses the target component (producer). Only the selected specs pass.

action.description: The action the dependency represents. Without it, the action is "uses".

selectedSpecs.description: Ids of the specs that pass, from both the consumer and the producer.

implementation.description: The source component (implementation) takes on the specs of the target component (definition). Specs pass from the definition to the implementation only.

excludedSpecs.description: Ids of the definition's specs that don't pass to the implementation.

enforcement.description: The source check enforces the target spec.

derivation.description: The source spec (derived) is derived from the target spec (origin).
